name.evidence: Cover leaf (img1) red label: 'CASE NO. 294 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / SANTA ROSA GRANT / MARIA JESUS OLIVERA DE COTA ET AL / CLAIMANT'. Transcript p89 (Sup. Ct. mandate): 'The land hereby confirmed is situated in the County of Santa Barbara, and is known by the name of Santa Rosa'.

year.evidence: Grant decree, transcript p24: 'Monterrey 30 de Julio de 1839 ... se declaro a Don Francisco Cota dueno en propiedad del terreno conocido con el nombre de Sta. Rosa'. Confirmed by U.S. Supreme Court mandate reciting the District Court decree, transcript p89-90: 'the first by Manuel Jimeno, acting governor of said department, on the 30th day of July, 1839'. NOTE a SECOND (ampliacion) grant of 19 Nov 1845 by Pio Pico is also in the file (transcript pp.27, 30, 90) - the register's single year 1839 is the first grant and is correct as far as it goes.

governor.evidence: Grant decree, transcript p24: 'El Senor Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin Gobernador Interino del Departamento de las Californias asi lo mando, decreto y firmo de que doy fe. Manuel Jimeno.' Court decree, transcript p89-90: 'granted to the said Francisco Cota ... the first by Manuel Jimeno, acting governor of said department, on the 30th day of July, 1839, and the second by governor Pio Pico on the 19th day of November, 1845.' Alvarado appears in this file ONLY on the later order of 10 June 1840 (transcript p25): 'El Sr. D. Juan B. Alvarado Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias asi lo proveyo y firmo... Alvarado' - i.e. he ordered the testimonio of the Assembly's approval issued in confirmation of the terreno 'que otorgo en treinta de Julio de mil ochocientos treinta y nueve'. He did not make the concession.

grantee.evidence: Register holds the U.S.-era CLAIMANT, not the Mexican grantee. Transcript p18, stipulation of J. J. Warner: 'he was acquainted with Don Francisco Cota the original grantee in the above entitled cause ... the present claimant Dona Maria Jesus Olivera de Cota is the widow of the said original grantee'. Grant decree p24: 'se declaro a Don Francisco Cota dueno en propiedad del terreno'. Expediente cover, transcript p20: 'Expediente sobre el Paraje nombrado Santa Rosa. Solicitado por Francisco Cota.' Court decree p89: 'the same land which was granted to the said Francisco Cota'.

outcome.evidence: Board confirmed 27 Feb 1855 (index of proceedings, transcript p3: 'Commissioner R. Aug. Term 1863 No. 138, affirmed 'to the extent of three and one half square leagues of land and no more' (transcript p91), mandate filed 7 July 1868 (p93); District Court decree on mandate, transcript pp.84-87, Ogden Hoffman Dist. Judge. No patent copy in the file.

corrections.governor: Manuel Jimeno (Jimeno Casarin), gobernador interino / acting governor, 30 July 1839 - per grant decree transcript p24 and U.S. court decree transcript p89-90; second grant 19 Nov 1845 by Pio Pico. NOT Alvarado.
corrections.grantee: Francisco Cota (Don Francisco Cota) - per grant decree transcript p24, expediente cover p20, Warner stipulation p18. 'Maria Jesus Olivera de Cota' is his widow and the U.S.-era claimant.

notes: Hoffman 1862 agrees with the case file against the register on BOTH flagged/erroneous fields (Hoffman: grantee 'Francisco Cota'; governor 'Manuel Jimeno, and 2 leagues November 19th, 1845, by Pio Pico'). Digicoll record 102019 has NO cubanc_lcf_sd294.pdf - only 95 JPEG leaves; the digicoll server returns HTTP 200 with text/html for any missing file, so a naive curl -sIL check on the .pdf URL falsely reads as 200. name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 56 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / YSLA DE SANTA ROSA GRANT / MANUEL[A] CARRILLO DE JONES, ET AL / CLAIMANT'. District Court decree, transcript p131: 'the lands of which confirmation is made is the Island of Santa Rosa in the County of Santa Barbara'.

year.evidence: Grant title, transcript p8 (Spanish original) closes: 'Dada en Monterey a cuatro de Octubre de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y tres. Manl. Micheltna. Manl. Jimeno Srio.' Sworn translation, transcript pp.15-16 ('B. Translation of Grant'): 'Given at Monterey on the fourth of October one thousand eight hundred & forty three (Signed) Manuel Micheltorena (Signed) Manuel Jimeno Secretary'. Petition, transcript p4: 'That on the 4th day of October A.D. 1843 Manuel Micheltorena Governor of California ... granted to Jose Antonio Carrillo & Carlos Carrillo the tract of land called the Island of Santa Rosa'. Nothing dated 1841 appears anywhere in the pages read.

governor.evidence: The only granting officer in the file is Micheltorena. Transcript p8: 'Manuel Micheltorena General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano Gobernador y Comandante General del departamento de ambas Californias ... he venido en concederle exclusivte. la Isla mencionada declarandoles la propriedad de ella por las presentes letras'. Translation p15: 'Manuel Micheltorena General of Brigade of the Mexican Army Governor & commanding General of the Department of Both Californias ... I have granted to them exclusively the said Island'. Alvarado does not appear in the grant, the petition, the deed of transfer, or the judicial possession; 'Manuel Jimeno' appears only as Secretary countersigning.

grantee.evidence: Register holds the PURCHASER/claimant. Grant, transcript p8: 'Por Cuanto Dn. Jose Antonio y D. Carlos Carillo, han pretendido para su beneficios personales y el de sus familias la Isla nombrada Santa Rosa'. Translation p15: 'Whereas Don Jose Antonio & Don Carlos Carillo have for their own personal benefit and that of their families petitioned for the Island called Santa Rosa'. Manuela Carrillo de Jones and Francisca Carrillo de Thompson BOUGHT the island from the two Carrillos by escritura of 2 Nov 1843 for $3,300 (transcript pp.9-11 Spanish, pp.17-19 translation). Claimants' brief, transcript p121: 'The grant was to Jose Antonio Carrillo and Carlos Carrillo: The Commissioners entirely overlooked the conveyance (& translation) from them the grantees to Manuela Carrillo de Jones and Francisca Carrillo de Thompson.'

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 56 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 'LAND CASE 56 SD PAGES 132'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd056.pdf; every leaf stamped '56 SD PAGE n'. Land Commission docket no. 117 (transcript p1, p2), matching Hoffman's commission_no 117.

outcome.evidence: The Board REJECTED: transcript p3, 'San Francisco Nov 1st 1853. In the same case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the opinion of the Board rejecting the claim'; index of case, transcript p121, 'Remark: The title was rejected by the Commissioners ... because the present claimants did not connect themselves with the title'. But the U.S. District Court, S.D. Cal., Dec. Term 1856, Hon. Isaac S. K. Ogier, decreed (transcript p131): 'It is ordered adjudged and decreed that the decision of the Commissioners be and the same is hereby REVERSED, and that the claim of the said Appellants is good and valid, and the same is hereby Confirmed to them, the lands of which confirmation is made is the Island of Santa Rosa in the County of Santa Barbara'. The U.S. appeal to the Supreme Court was vacated by stipulation and the decree made final (transcript pp.125-126, 129-130, filed 5 Feb 1857); Attorney General's letter of 18 Sept 1856, transcript p127: 'appeal in the Supreme Court will not be prosecuted by the United States.' Register's 'Confirmed' is right on the final decree. No patent copy in the file.

corrections.governor: Manuel Micheltorena, alone (transcript p8/p15). Alvarado has no part in this grant.
corrections.grantee: Jose Antonio Carrillo and Carlos (Antonio) Carrillo, brothers (transcript p8/p15). Manuela Carrillo de Jones is a purchaser under the 2 Nov 1843 deed and the U.S.-era claimant.

The red case label spells the claimant 'MANUEL CARRILLO DE JONES' (a binder's slip for Manuela). PDF is 116 MB / 141 images; I read it via pypdf page-range excerpts.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 346 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / SANTIAGO GRANT / YORBA PERALTA, ET AL / CLAIMANT'; transcript p1 'for the place named "Santiago"'. The two names are the same tract: Sepulveda deposition, transcript p8, 'The Rancho now called Santa Ana is the same as that formerly called Santiago'; Coronel, transcript p9, 'The Rancho has also been known by the name of Santiago'; District Court summons, transcript p54, 'the land called "Santiago or Santa Anna" situate in the County of Los Angeles'.

year.evidence: Petition, transcript p5: 'they claim said Land in Virtue of a Concession thereof to the said Antonio Yorba and the said Juan Pablo Peralta made by Arrillaga Governor of the Province of California in pursuance of an Authority in him vested and bearing date Sept 1st 1810.' The expediente translation carries Arrillaga's own decrees of 'Monterey March 26th 1810' (order of reference) and the concession, transcript p21: 'Monterey July 1st 1810. There is no embarrassment on my part that there may be conceded to him the tract of "Santiago" which he solicits ... Arrillaga.' Santiago Arguello, transcript p10: 'A paper is now shown me purporting to be the title papers to Antonio Yorba and Juan Pablo Peralta the last date to which is Sepr 1. 1810.' 1810 is right; the file shows the concession decree itself is dated 1 July 1810 and the title/possession papers run to 1 Sept 1810.

governor.evidence: Right in kind but unnamed. The granting officer is Jose Joaquin de Arrillaga: concession decree, transcript p21, 'Monterey July 1st 1810 ... Arrillaga'; reference decree, transcript p20, 'Monterey March 26th 1810. Let this be passed to the Lieutenant D. Franco Ma Ruiz ... Arrillaga'; Santiago Arguello, transcript p10, 'The two signatures Arrillaga on said paper I believe to be genuine signatures of said Jose Joaquin Arrillaga. He was at the date of said papers Governor of California'; petition, transcript p5, 'made by Arrillaga Governor of the Province of California'. The register's 'a Spanish governor' is correct as far as it goes (Arrillaga was the Spanish-era governor) but names nobody.

grantee.evidence: Register holds the U.S.-era claimants. Petition, transcript p5: 'The Petition of the Heirs and Legal representatives of Antonio Yorba deceased and Juan Pablo Peralta deceased'. Stipulation with the U.S. Law Agent, transcript p23: 'the United States will not take any objections to the confirmation being made to the Heirs and Legal Representatives of Antonio Yorba and Juan Pablo Peralta.' District Court summons, transcript p54 and p58: 'To Bernardo Yorba, Theodocio Yorba and Ramon Yorba, The Heirs of Antonio Yorba and Juan Pablo Peralta' - i.e. the register's three names are expressly identified in the file as HEIRS, not grantees. Ruiz's report in the expediente, transcript p21, recommends 'that the invalid Sargent Antonio Yorba should live in said Rancho in company with his children and her grandson Juan Pablo Peralta'.

year.evidence: The grant title, transcript pp.36-37, closes: 'Es dado en Monterrey del Departamento de las Californias a once de Febrero de mil ocho cientos treinta y ocho. Juan B. Alvarado. Franco. name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 343 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / SHOQUEL GRANT / MARTINA CASTRO / CLAIMANT'; transcript p1 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Shoquel"'. The augmentation is named throughout: Guadalupe Castro depo., transcript p11, 'the tract of Land claimed in this Case lying in Santa Cruz County and known as the Augmentation to the "Rancho de Soquel"'; Juan Jose Castro, transcript p16, 'the boundaries are on one side the place known as "Palo de la Yesca" so called from an Oak tree that formerly stood there from which punk was obtained'; District Court depo. of Francisco Alviso, transcript p78, 'the augmentation grant of Martina Castro in Santa Cruz Co. Cala.'

year.evidence: The augmentation expediente is entirely of 1844. Martina Castro's petition, transcript pp.25/30: 'suplico a V.E. libra mandar se agregue al titulo nuevo que pido, la tierra inmediata al rancho que actualmente poseo, conocida con el nombre del Palo de la Yesca que se halla enteramente baldia. Monterrey 7 de Enero de 1844.' Micheltorena's order of reference, transcript p25: 'Monterey, En.o 11 de 1844. Inf.e el S. Srio del despacho teniendo antes los convenientes. Micheltorena.' Alviso's informe 'Sta Cruz 23 de Enero de 1844'; Jimeno's informe 'Monterrey 8 de Febrero de 1844'; Micheltorena's decree, transcript pp.26/31: 'Monterey Fbro. 9 de 1844. Confe con el anterior informe dense las ordenes...' and, same date, Jimeno's execution order, transcript pp.27/32: 'ocurra la interesada al Juez de Branciforte a quien se le ordena, ponga en posesion a Da Martina Castro de toda la extension que pretende de la Sierra de la Yesca hasta la laguna del Sanjuento y la chuchita, incluyendo la loma Prieta.' Also a Micheltorena decree of '7 de Enero de 1844' on her Oct. 1843 petition, transcript p29/p35. The Board petition, transcript p6, alleges '17th of January 1844'. Every candidate date is in 1844, so the register's 1844 stands.

governor.evidence: For the AUGMENTATION the granting governor is Micheltorena alone (decrees quoted above, transcript pp.25-27 / 30-32, all signed 'Micheltorena', countersigned 'Manuel Jimeno'). Figueroa granted the UNDERLYING Soquel rancho, which is also in this same case file: concession decree, transcript p20, 'Monterrey Nov.re 22 de 1833 ... se declara a Martina de Castro duena en propiedad del terreno conocido con el nombre de Soquel ... El Sr. D. Jose Figueroa Comandte Genl Inspector y Gefe Superior Politico del Territorio de la Alta California asi lo mando, decreto y firmo de que doy fe. Jose Figueroa'; titulo, transcript p22, 'Jose Figueroa Genl de Brigada de los Ejercitos Nacionales Mejicanos ... Por cuanto Martina Castro, esposa de Miguel Lodge, ha pretendido ... el terreno conocido con el nombre de Soquel'; Assembly approval 17 May 1834 and Figueroa's confirming decree 'Monterey Agosto 2 de 1834', transcript p24. So the register's pair of governors describes the case file correctly but is imprecise for a record titled 'Augmentation', where only Micheltorena granted.

grantee.evidence: Right person, abbreviated. The grantee of both the 1833 rancho and the 1844 augmentation is MARTINA Castro: transcript p18 expediente cover, 'Espediente sobre el paraje nombrado Shoquel solicitado pa su ocupacion y beneficio por Martin[a] de Castro'; 1833 titulo, transcript p22, 'Por cuanto Martina Castro, esposa de Miguel Lodge'; 1844 petition, transcript p30, 'Martina Castro de la vecindad de la villa de Branciforte'; District Court caption throughout, transcript pp.76-88, 'The United States vs Martina Castro'. 'M. Castro' is ambiguous in a file that also contains Rafael Castro (an adjoining owner, transcript p28), Guadalupe Castro and Juan Jose Castro (witnesses, transcript pp.11, 15).

corrections.governor: For the augmentation: Manuel Micheltorena alone (transcript pp.25-27/30-32). Jose Figueroa belongs to the 1833/1834 Soquel grant that underlies it (transcript pp.20-24).

notes: Hoffman's flagged year 1834 is NOT a disagreement about the augmentation: Hoffman's own governor column for this row reads 'Jose Figueroa, and surplus lands, known as Palo de la Yesca, described by boundaries, granted January 7th, 1844, by Manuel Micheltorena' - i.e. Hoffman's 1834 is the Figueroa grant and he dates the surplus to 1844, agreeing with the register. Note ND 343 (Board 593) litigated BOTH the 1833/34 Soquel rancho and the 1844 augmentation in one transcript, so a register that splits them into two rows will point both at this same case file. The 1844 file is unusually contentious: the alcalde Francisco Alviso admits in the District Court (transcript p79) that he first 'reported adversely to the grant' on the representation of hostile neighbours and then 'reported a second time and then in favor of the grant'; a U.S. examiner's marginal note at transcript pp.26/31 alleges that words in the informe 'were evidently written originally "no" and have subsequently been maliciously changed into "se"'. name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 103 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / SAN JUAN [recte JOSE] DE GRACIA ALIAS SIMI GRANT / JOSE DE LA GUERRA Y NORIEGA / CLAIMANT'; transcript p1 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "San Jose de Gracia, alias Simi"'; Doc No.1, transcript p13, 'este rancho de San Jose de Gracia y Simi'; Surveyor General's certificate, transcript p87, 'the Rancho "Simi" confirmed to J. de la Guerra y Noriega'.

year.evidence: Doc No.1 (the three brothers' 1821 petition, annexed to Santiago Arguello's deposition), transcript p13: 'pues este dicho rancho esta dado por el Sor. Gobor. Dn. Diego de Borica q. de Dios goze el ano de 1795'. Governor Sola's ratifying decree on the same paper, transcript p14: 'Monterrey 8 de Marzo de 1821 ... teniendo en consideracion lo dispuesto pr. mi antecesor el Sor Coronel D. Diego de Borica en favor de Patricio Pico, Jabier Pico y Miguel Pico del rancho nombrado Simi q. poseen hace la epoca de veinte y seis anos les ratifico esto mismo' - twenty-six years before 1821 is 1795, an internal check. Petition, transcript p5: 'That in the year 1795, Diego Borica, Governor of California, granted to the brothers Patricio Pico, Javier Pico and Miguel Pico, the tract of land called "Simi"'. The original 1795 title was LOST (transcript p5, 'the said title having been lost'), which is why the brothers sought the 1821 replacement.

governor.evidence: Diego de Borica, named in the file's own documents: Doc No.1, transcript p13, 'esta dado por el Sor. Gobor. Dn. Diego de Borica q. de Dios goze el ano de 1795'; Sola's decree, transcript p14, 'lo dispuesto pr. mi antecesor el Sor Coronel D. Diego de Borica'. Sola (1821) and Alvarado (1842 regrant to de la Guerra, petition transcript p5) are later actors, not the 1795 grantor.

grantee.evidence: The three Pico brothers. Doc No.1, transcript p13: 'Patricio Pico, Jabier Pico y Miguel Pico todos los nombrados hermanos se presentan con el debido respeto y sumision', signed at transcript p14 'Patricio Pico / Jabier Pico / Miguel Pico'; Sola's decree, transcript p14, 'en favor de Patricio Pico, Jabier Pico y Miguel Pico del rancho nombrado Simi'. The register has correctly recorded the MEXICAN/SPANISH grantees and NOT the U.S.-era claimant (Jose de la Guerra y Noriega, who bought the rancho from Rafael Pico as attorney for his uncles in 1832-42; escritura at transcript pp.15-23).

The U.S. filed a petition for review (answer of appellee, transcript p81A, served 27 Dec 1855) and the District Court ordered the transcript returned for amendment (transcript p85, filed 17 Dec 1855), but the appeal was abandoned: Attorney General's letter, transcript p83, '29 September 1856 ... In the case of the claim of Jose de la Guerra y Noriega, confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, Case no. thirty-eight (38), appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States'; endorsement, transcript p84, '(not prosd Dist Court) Dismissed Dec. 20. 56'. Survey followed: Surveyor General's certificates, transcript pp.87-90, 'the Rancho "Simi" confirmed to J. de la Guerra y Noriega has been surveyed by this office, and ... the survey and plat was approved by the U.S. Surveyor General, on the 19th day of March 1861', published 1862-63, filed 1864-65. notes: REGISTER CORRECT ON ALL SIX FIELDS; HOFFMAN'S 1842 IS THE WRONG GRANT for a row describing the original Simi title. Hoffman's year column (1842) is the date of Alvarado's ratification/regrant to the purchaser Jose de la Guerra y Noriega (petition, transcript p5: 'on the 25th day of April A.D. 1842, Juan B. Alvarado, then Governor of California, by virtue of power in him vested, ratified & confirmed the said purchase and sale, and regranted the said tract of land to the petitioner'); Hoffman's governor and grantee cells for this row are blank, so there is no Hoffman reading to prefer. TWO CAVEATS a re-reader should know. (1) The register's grantee string 'Patricio Javier y Miguel Pico' lacks a comma and can be misread as two men; the file names THREE brothers - Patricio Pico, Javier (Jabier) Pico and Miguel Pico - so the preferred form is 'Patricio, Javier y Miguel Pico'. (2) An internal conflict about who first received Simi in 1795: the 1832 escritura de venta, transcript p22, says the rancho 'graciosamente obtuvo del Gobierno del Territorio antiguamente el abuelo paterno del vendedor Santiago Pico, y posteriormente se ratifico la concesion por el mismo Gobierno a su difunto padre Patricio Pico y tios expresados' - i.e. the grandfather SANTIAGO PICO got it and the concession was only later ratified to Patricio and his brothers. The 1821 papers (the nearest surviving substitute for the lost 1795 title, and the documents on which the Board acted) put the Borica grant in the three brothers' names; the 1832 deed puts it in Santiago Pico's. I have not resolved this and flag it rather than pick a side. PDF is 98 MB / 102 images.

It was. I have sold it and conveyed it by deed, and now have no interest in it whatever. The Ranch was granted to me by the name of the Soulajille Ranch. Q3. Why was it called Ramon Mesa Ranch? A. I changed the name and called it after myself.' John Martin, transcript p61: 'I know the Ranch by that name, and also by another name. The other name was the Ranch of Ramon Mesa.' outcome.evidence: The Board REJECTED: transcript p3, 'San Francisco April 17, 1855. In the same Case Commissioner R. Aug. Cornwell appealed - notice of appeal, transcript p37, 'the claimant in this case intends to prosecute an appeal from the decision of the Board of the United States Land Commission, rejecting his claim', filed 22 Dec 1855; petition of appeal, transcript pp.39-40, praying 'a reversal of the decision of the Board and that his title may be confirmed by the proper decree' and stating the ground of rejection ('the claim was rejected by the Board on the ground that the Ranch was called "Soulajulle" in the grant, while in the Mesne Conveyances it was called "San Ramon"'); U.S. answer denying validity, transcript p42. corrections.grantee: Jose Ramon Mesa (transcript pp.4, 6, 39, 58, 62). George N. Cornwell took by mesne conveyances of 6 Dec 1849 and 6 Aug 1850 and is the U.S.-era claimant.

notes: Hoffman 1862 agrees with the case file against the register: grantee is Ramon Mesa. Year (1844) and governor (Micheltorena) in the register are correct. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL POINT for the register: the single Micheltorena grant of 29 March 1844 to Jose Ramon Mesa was broken up by sale into FIVE separate U.S. land cases, all of Soulajule and all with different claimants - ND 328 (George N. Cornwell), ND 329 (Joshua L. Brackett), ND 331 (Pedro J. Vasquez), ND 334 (Martin J. Gormly), ND 352 (Lewis D. Watkins) - see transcript p57 and pp.54-55. So the register's two Soulajule rows (Cornwell ND 328 and Watkins ND 352) are two of five, and in every one of them the correct grantee is the same man, Jose Ramon Mesa. Note also that the ORIGINAL grant paper is not in this transcript: the petition, transcript p5, says 'The original grant of said land is filed in the case of Joshua L. Brackett No ___ to which you are referred', and the grant was proved here by Mesa's deposition taken in Board case 233 (Brackett) and by Larkin in the District Court. My year/governor citations therefore rest on the pleadings plus two sworn identifications of the original grant, not on the decree text itself, which is in the Brackett file (ND 329).
